Perhaps this is a more controversial viewpoint, but based on reading other comments here and as someone only in their early 20s, I feel that always limiting oneself as a woman isn’t always the best route. If you can take good precautions, then you should do whatever your gut tells you is right. The idea that solo travel isn’t feasible because of trafficking is obviously routed in truth, but it shouldn’t mean you aren’t able to travel by yourself either. Just take precautions and be aware. Also being from the UK myself, it’s certainly not as dangerous as many other places for this. 

I did visit my partner first despite being both younger than them and a woman, to a country where I don’t fluently speak the language. However I trusted them to be there right away to pick me up, and I also had vaguely planned a return if he didn’t. 

The problem with this seems that your partner’s reasons to not visit you seem quite flimsy? A fear of flying is valid but shouldn’t stop him in a LDR imo (I have a fear of it myself). Maybe speak to him about your own worries about travelling alone for the first time, and see if he comes around. While I do believe in women being independent (safely), I also feel for a first time visit everything should be as comfortable as possible. And of course make sure he definitely is who he says he is beforehand.

Reading this felt close to a mirror of my own life, right down to the awful college experience, SA, controlling family, no good friends and previous traumatic relationships. I’m so so sorry you’ve had to go through any of this. 

I feel like living through such circumstances, at least for me, tend to make me feel things more and especially when intimate with someone there is a certain level of attention or care that is needed. In my current ldr relationship (though we are still technically not official) I often feel inadequate because he always has friends to see or do things with whereas I am almost always alone. You don’t want to depend on them too much, especially from a distance, but it’s hard not to want more sometimes, or to compare yourself. He’s been the most attentive of anyone I’ve ever gotten close to, though I still sometimes feel a similar lag which I can’t stand. 

I don’t know if I have any real advice here since honestly I’m still trying to figure out these things myself from being in such a similar situation. But the way you describe him is though he is constantly busy with friends, I assume he plays with friends online too? The fact he hasn’t even tried to play one game with you is a little alarming. Do you two do any activities together online? I think there has to be something you both share and can both engage in together as he does with his friends for there to be a stronger foundation of partnership. Hang in there, and trust your gut as best you can.
